judgment_calls: Split the meta commentary (L2397-2398) into two nodes (n008, n009) based on the split test: 'developers can customize broadly' and 'some forms of deception violate policies' are independently true/false claims. Could have kept as one meta-commentary node for simpler structure.

Included n001 (heading metadata with authority=user) as a content node, establishing the permission-level scope of the section. This is similar to the n010 pattern in the worked example (charter rules). Alternative: mark as uncovered and treat authority=user as implicit.

n002 needs both objective_truth_seeking (inherited from parent's prior child) and section_user_authority (from n001), showing how user permissions override default objective behavior. Could have omitted section_user_authority since the rule is semantically clear without it.

All five examples (n003-n007) need user_perspective_spectrum_permission from n002, demonstrating different scenarios: specific side, violent extremist, counter-argument, creator criticism, and developer override. Each is a worked example per the brief. Considered grouping conceptually but example-by-example decomposition better follows the guidance.

n008 needs user_perspective_spectrum_permission to establish that developer customization extends the same capability granted to users. The commentary text 'in this way' explicitly links developer behavior to the user-requested permission. Could have made developer customization independent.

usage_policies is left as a dangling need in n009 (external reference). This is honest about scope: the section references but does not establish the deception policies. Parent or sibling span must provide this concept or escalate.
